Keeping the Light: Autumn Notes

By Marta Ellison, keeper of the Gull Rock light

The autumn watch begins when the swallows leave the cliff ledges, and from that evening the lamp is lit a full hour earlier than the almanac table suggests, because the fog comes in faster than the printed tide columns allow for and a ship feeling her way along the Gull Rock channel needs the light before she needs the harbour.

Every keeper learns the same lesson in the first season: the lamp is the easy part. The work is the logbook, the lens cloth, the brass that tarnishes if you so much as look at it during a salt storm, and the stairs, one hundred and twelve of them, twice a night in the blowing months when the wind tries the door at the top.

Stores for the season

  • Lamp oil, two casks, winter grade
  • Spare wicks, trimmed and waxed
  • Matches in the tin above the stove
